channel.title: Comments on: See No Evil
channel.description: taoism, taoist thought, buddha, yoga, tai chi, shakuhachi

item.title: By: carl
item.dc:creator: carl
item.description:
Oh I won't be closing down the site, at least not in my foreseeable future. Even as I tapper off blogging, I'd keep posting the Chapters of the Tao Te Ching. And even if tapper off that, I'd still keep the site up as a kind of reference. So no worries.
Nuts indeed! I suppose that is why Buddha said Right Attention. Certainly, attention focused on the object of one's needs/fears (desires/worries)drowns out 'wide screen awareness'. On the other hand though, each life form's strength is also its greatest weakness. Thinking is our dynamic duo.
While we have our difficulties, there is no other species I'd rather be. Of course, my duck say there is no other species they would trade places with either. Family bonds are strong.

item.title: By: Lynn cornish
item.dc:creator: Lynn cornish
item.description:
I always click on your facebook posts to see what you have to say. I was just on my way to read about the rock. I don't always comment but I am sure happy you are writing. I know that one day you will stop but give us some advance notice so we can print everything out.
One of my Facebook friends had an epiphany that awareness is different from attention because attention carries attachment and it reminded me of how much faith we put in language as if language is it, not the experience but the words are what's important or real. Nuts.

item.title: By: carl
item.dc:creator: carl
item.description:
Well it's unanimous then! I'll keep posting for awhile longer ;-)
I do sometimes wonder why I'm doing this. I began writing observations down years ago to better see what I was thinking. Or rather, think about what I was seeing. Basically, I attempt to understand in words what I feel, but have no words to match. Now, if in doing this, my writings help speak to what others also intuitively feel then this is a double win.
Another reason is that if my boys wonder what I'd say about such and such 50 years from now they can just Google it. The thing is, I am starting to feel I've said enough.
It also becomes increasingly difficult to write down the impartial 'big picture'. Beside, the years are bringing me ever closer to, as the Tao Te Ching say, the "<em>benefit of resorting to no action and the teaching that uses no words</em>". Or closer still, as chapter 23 puts it:
<blockquote>To use words but rarely is to be natural.
Hence a gusty wind cannot last all morning, and a sudden downpour cannot last all day. Who is it that produces these? Heaven and earth. If even heaven and earth cannot go on for ever, much less can man. That is why one follows the way.</blockquote>

item.title: By: carl
item.dc:creator: carl
item.description:
Did you pick up a vibe from this end? I was wondering today about tapering off my posts here. Hearing your words gives me reason to continue awhile longer.
Yours is a good way to reset the clock, so to speak. Though I dare say there is an essential step that precedes your practice. That is being present enough to nip your 'self' in the bud. That just goes to show how years of meditation has paid off.

item.title: By: Lynn cornish
item.dc:creator: Lynn cornish
item.description:
Regarding letting go, I've learned a good practice that helps. It's so practical!
When you are feeling attraction or repulsion, take 30 seconds . Close your eyes if you can, pay attention to what you are feeling, surround your feelings with warmth and openness, open your eyes suddenly and jump back into the world.
Simple and it works to neutralize the pulls and pushes of life.
I find since I've been doing this I've been less reactive.
I've learned so much from you Carl that I already knew but your words have made it more accessible somehow. Thank you.
